title: Chapter 4. Srimati Jahnava Gosvamini's Journey to Vrindavana
html:
Virachandra's second marriage; Jahnava sets out for Vrindavana; Chandana Mandala of Mangalkot and his chariot; visions; praise of Nityananda (pp. 40–45)

[p. 40]

1Glory, glory to Nityananda, purifier of the fallen!
Glory to Virachandra, whose treasure is Nityananda!

2Glory to the life of the life of Vasudha and Jahnava!
Glory to Virachandra — that same son of Shachi1!

3Then Prabhu2 entered a second marriage,
with a most fortunate [maiden] named Vishnupriya3.

4In beauty, virtues and character she was Lakshmi in person;
Vasu and Jahnava rejoiced to see their daughter-in-law.

5Sri Jahnava mercifully made her a disciple,
and she surrendered herself to Prabhu's lotus feet.

6A great and faithful wife, she serves Virachandra,
and Narayani Devi loves her in every way.

7Like Lakshmi and Sarasvati — such is the way of the two:
lovingly they serve Virachandra, [Vishnupriya] and Narayani4.

8Narayani and Vishnupriya are both mothers of the world;
to Vasudha and Jahnava both are dear as life.

9The two daughters-in-law always serve the two mothers,
and Sri Vasu and Jahnava float in an ocean of happiness.

10Ever devoted to the service of Shyamasundara,
they serve Prabhu Virachandra with body and mind.

11Sri Virachandra Raya is Nityananda himself in essence;
by his power sin and unbelief take flight.

12His three sons5 are [the virtues] embodied:
peaceful, self-controlled, pure; their good qualities have no end.

13By the cool rays of Virachandra all living beings [are comforted];
I myself was comforted merely hearing of it from one another.

14Srimati Jahnava said to Virachandra:
"I am very pleased with your devotion.

15Give me leave, my son; I will go to Vrindavana:
my heart longs for the son of the lord of Vraja."

16Hearing this, Virachandra said with joined palms:
"For what offence, Prabhu6, will you go and leave [us]?

17You are surely the best of purushas and prakritis7;
you are the form of Radha and Krishna, there is no doubt.

18You are the Lord of Vrindavana and the Queen of Vrindavana;
you are Prabhu Nityananda, Gauranga, Sri Hari.

19You are Ananga Manjari8, the desire of my heart,
my perfected chosen deity, firm in bhava9.

20What can I say to this? You are independent.
To go is your wish; such is everyone's […]10.

21If you go, Prabhu, my life will in no way remain.
Holding your feet, Prabhu, I implore you:

22I will go with you, gazing at Prabhu's feet —
for what should I stay in worldly life?"

[p. 41]

23Prabhu said: "It is not the time for you to go.
Later you will come to your own abode."11

24Gosani accepted the order, placing it on his head,
and auspicious sounds arose, filling heaven and earth.

25With many male and female servants, with many Vaishnavas,
she set out on her auspicious journey — a great festival.

26Gopijanavallabha Gosani12, seeing her off,
brought and set at the door a splendidly decked palanquin.

27The Mother of the world joyfully mounted the palanquin;
all the Vaishnavas go along, calling the name of Hari.

28Crossing the Ganga, they go along the bank of the Ganga
to Kantaka-nagara, the place where Prabhu was shaven13.

29For three days a great festival was held there,
and many Vaishnavas came and joined them there.

30She ordered: "I will go by the road through Radha14,
to [see] first of all, with love, Prabhu's birthplace."15

31On the way there is [a village] named Mangalkot;
in that village lives a merchant, Chandana Mandala.

32That wealthy Vaishnava, his mind fixed on the highest goal,
had built a chariot with great care.

33Hearing that Prabhu was going to Vrindavana-dhama,
he said, "I have attained my goal; my desire is fulfilled!"

34With all his family he went there, a cloth around his neck16,
and lay down, blocking Prabhu's path.

35Prabhu asked: "What is this? Why is he lying on the road?"
Then Thakura Ramai17 reported at her feet:

36"He is a worldly man of the merchant caste, his name is Chandana;
a servant of your house, he lays a petition before you."

37Hearing this, Prabhu said: "Get up, say: Krishna, Krishna!
Prabhu will fulfil the desire of your heart."

38Hearing this, Mandala rises and dances, crying "Hari, Hari!"
He dances, sings, weeps, falls and rolls on the ground.

39Crying "Glory to Nityananda!" he roars aloud;
his whole body thrills, tears stream from his eyes.

40By [her] mercy his body became full of grace.
The order was given: "Let us all go to Mandala's house."

[p. 42]

41Hearing this, the householder rejoiced
and with his people busily prepared the auspicious [celebration].

42He spread new washed cloth on the road,
set full new pots at the door and planted plantain trees.

43Stringing mango leaves into garlands,
he lit ghee lamps at every door.

44Incense, lamps, sandal, garlands — the sixteen offerings:
all things for the puja were set at the door of the pavilion.

45A cot-seat, pitchers filled with fragrant water,
fans, chamaras, new sandals and the like.

46His house, wife, sons, life, wealth and people
he offered without guile at Prabhu's feet.

47"Ah, my, my Nityananda Raya!" —
he laughs, weeps, dances, falls and sings only this.

48Crying "Krishna Chaitanya!" his heart trembles;
crying "O Vasu and Jahnava!" he sobs aloud.

49In joy his house filled with people,
and all at once everyone saw the manifestation [of her nature].

50Some see her four-armed, some eight-armed,
some see Brahma, Shiva and others worshipping her.

51Some see her in the form of Durga, some as Jahnavi18,
some in the form of Gayatri, some as Vaishnavi.

52Some see purusha and prakriti in a single abode,
some see her lovely, in her form of bliss.

53Some see Krishna, some see Balarama,
some see the Queen of Vrindavana, abode of radiance.

54Some see the leader of the groups of gopis, the chief prakriti,
while the gopis play instruments, dance and sing.

55Some see the dark, glossy Balarama19
playing in the pastures in the company of his friend Sridama.

56Each sees according to the bhava in his own heart;
the eternally perfected receive a wondrous vision.

57Thus Nityananda manifests himself;
whoever does not accept this is very wicked.

58What need have I of such people?
I do not look at the face of those without faith in Nityananda.

59He is the guru of the five rasas, mantra embodied,
the vessel of Krishna's happiness, whose qualities have no end.

60As a servant he massages Krishna's feet;
as a friend he is all-knowing, his words full of trust20.

61In parental love he feels great tenderness for Krishna;
in sweet [love] his own shaktis are all the beloveds.

62Radhika, in the form of Ananga, is the chief prakriti;
she delights Krishna, and so she is the hladini shakti.

63In the form of the chief prakriti he21 himself serves [Krishna]
whenever Krishna desires service.

64Servitude, friendship, parental love, the love of a beloved in Vrindavana —
whoever wants any of these, let him worship Nitai's feet.

65All of Krishna's lilas, of majesty and of sweetness,
are nourished by the son of Rohini22.

66Dharma, artha, moksha, kama, kingdom, wealth, a wife23 —
whatever one wants, one will obtain it all without hindrance.

67He descends to save the fallen —
whoever lacks bhakti for such a Nityananda is worthless.

68What business have I with such people?
The treasure of my life is ever Nityananda Raya.

69[He is the body] in which Gaurachandra sports;
apart from bhakti to Nityananda there is nothing.

70Whoever has no faith in such a Nityananda
is ruined both in this life and in the next.

[p. 43]

71The body of being, consciousness and bliss, named Radha and Krishna —
those two are now one: Nityananda-Rama.

72It is also said in the Brahmanda Purana, in the dialogue of Earth and Shesha24:
"Nitya, 'the eternal', is the name of Sri Radhika; Ananta is the form of Krishna;
the two united, O Earth, are named Nityananda."

73If my words do not inspire faith,
look in the dialogue of Earth and Shesha — you will find it plainly stated.

74Those with bhakti accept this firmly;
non-devotees, even seeing the shastra, do not accept the truth.

75Thus Sri Jahnava for twelve years25
held great festivals, ready to move on.

76An announcement went out to all the Vaishnavas,
and all said: "Get ready, get ready!"

77Mandala came and, with a cloth around his neck, said:
"For three more days, Prabhu, I will not let you go.

78By your mercy I have built a chariot,
and to this day I have not dedicated it even to Vishnu.

79You are Krishna himself; have mercy on me,
put aside disdain and mount the chariot.

80Then the desire of my heart will be fulfilled,
and the name 'Purifier of the fallen' will remain proclaimed."

81Mandala's wife and sons fall at her feet
and, holding straws between their teeth26, surrender themselves:

82"You are the mother of the world, all are your children;
small and great, low and high — you protect them all.

83O, O mother of the world! We take refuge in you;
have mercy on this servant, fulfil his wish."

84Hearing his praise and devotion, Prabhu laughed
and gave an order to Gopijanavallabha Gosani:

85"Mount the chariot and deliver Mandala:
let him, with all his line, attain the highest destination.

86Especially since he is the object of mercy of the Lord of my life27;
knowing that bond, my child, fulfil his wish."

87"As you command," said Gosani, placing the order on his head,
and, recognizing him as a servant, fulfilled his wish.

88Playfully Prabhu28 mounted the chariot,
and on all sides all the people call the name of Hari.

89"Hari bol, Hari bol! Glory to Krishna and Rama!" —
this nectarean sound, the name of Krishna, rains down ceaselessly.

90Mounting the chariot, he revealed his own power:
a forest garland, yellow garments — he became four-armed.

91The high, the middling and the common people
all together, at one moment, received this vision.

92And he spread yet another power of mercy:
on everyone's lips words of praise, from their eyes streams of tears.

93Seated on the chariot, Prabhu accepted Mandala's puja
and cast his glance over the many prepared offerings.

94Mandala pulls the chariot together with his people,
and all the other people pull, holding the ropes.

95Mridangas and mandiras sound, karatalas are struck,
conches, bells, horns, bheris, damarus and khanjanis.

96In great joy all the people call the name of Hari;
at the sight [of Prabhu] the threefold miseries and grief went far away.

97By Prabhu's mercy no one feels hunger or thirst;
the merciful Gosani himself calls out and says:

98"The third watch of the day has come29;
everyone has toiled hard in the kirtana on the road.

99Bathe, drink, and all of you stay in this place;
today, day and night, perform the sankirtana of Krishna."

[p. 44]

100Everyone cried out: "We stay, we stay!"
Mandala came and fell at Prabhu's feet.

101Prabhu stepped down from the chariot and touched the earth —
such a merciful lila I have never heard of.

102Mandala says: "Prabhu, you are merciful.
All the land you passed over riding the chariot —

103this land is now your possession;
it has become a holy place; I have no more claim to it."

104Smiling slightly, Prabhu accepted [the gift];
all this news was brought and told to Srimati30.

105The place, with its trees wrapped in creepers, is charming;
when a sripat was founded there, it received the name Latadhama31.

106Prabhu transmitted his power there;
for the sake of lila many images and many holy places came to be.

107Kali is a maddened elephant; Prabhu's descendants are lions,
entitled to deliver souls in place after place.

108On this path [some] steal, putting on the guise of sadhus,
and teach mantras and Vedas in this world.

109Presenting themselves to others as Prabhu,
they sink and perish in the Raurava hell together with their servants.

110The names of such heretics are not [counted] among Prabhu's people;
everyone will see [their] deeds and their causes32.

111For the deliverance of people, for learning and the discernment of dharma,
Prabhu spread his descendants in the Kali age.

112The fallen, the wretched and the poor of the world
Nityananda diligently delivers.

113In purifying the fallen Nityananda is the utmost limit;
yet unbelievers and the wicked say: "What glory is there?"

114Looking, they cannot see his essential power,
just as the owl does not see the rays of the sun.

115Whoever bears enmity towards such a Nityananda,
on his head I set my foot.

116Reviling Prabhu, he destroys himself and dies;
there is no one in the world to save him.

117Nityananda Prabhu alone is the guru of the world,
the Lord himself, a wish-fulfilling tree for those who long for bhakti.

118Prabhu does not hold unbelief from ignorance as a fault;
[but] one who knowingly becomes an unbeliever and reviles him perishes.

119What concern is it of mine? They will perish on their own.
May my mind stay firm at Prabhu's feet.

120Glory, glory to Nityananda Prabhu, glory, glory!
I have sold myself without price at his feet.

121I have no refuge but Nityananda;
the treasure of my life is the son of Padmavati33.

122Glory, glory to Gaurachandra, son of Shachi,
by whose mercy I have attained Nityananda's feet!

123Glory, glory [to you], father Vishvambhara, Gaurahari!
May I never forget you, together with Nityananda.

124Glory to Vishvambhara, the life of my lord!
Always shine forth within me and without.

125What refuge have I but Gaura and Nityananda?
Birth after birth may these two brothers be my lords.

126O all you Vaishnavas, fulfil my hope:
may I be birth after birth a servant of Nityananda.

127And one more prayer I offer everywhere:
may I never see the face of one averse to Nityananda.

128May my mind remain at the feet of Prabhu Virachandra;
the feet of Sri Vasu and Jahnava are the treasure of my life.

129Hoping for the feet of Virachandra Prabhu,
Vrindavana Dasa tells the Vamsha-vistara.

[p. 45]

Thus ends, in the Madhya-lila of the Vamsha-vistara of Sri Sri Nityananda Prabhu, the fourth chapter, called "Srimati Jahnava Gosvamini's Journey to Sri Sri Vrindavana".

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. That is, Virachandra is Gauranga himself (the son of Shachi) appearing again (see Chapter 2).
  2. Here "Prabhu" is Virachandra.
  3. Vishnupriya, Virachandra's second wife (not to be confused with Vishnupriya, Chaitanya's consort); the first is Narayani.
  4. The end of the first line is restored from copy B ("do~hāra rīti"); A reads "hu dauhāra rinti". The sense of the second line is conjectural.
  5. By tradition Virachandra's sons are Gopijanavallabha, Ramakrishna and Ramachandra.
  6. Virachandra addresses Jahnava as "Prabhu", "Mistress"; in this chapter Jahnava is usually so called.
  7. That is, surpassing both the male and the female principle; cf. Chapter 2, couplet 5.
  8. Ananga Manjari, Radha's younger sister; Jahnava is held to be her incarnation.
  9. "bhāva niṣṭha siddha mora sanmita iṣṭa" — the word "sanmita/saśmita" is unclear; the translation is approximate.
  10. The line is corrupt: "yāite tomāra mukha (B: nakha) ei savāra mantra (B: manta)"; the sense of the second half is unclear.
  11. That is, to Vrindavana, the "own" abode of Ananga Manjari.
  12. Gopijanavallabha, Virachandra's son and Jahnava's grandson.
  13. Kantaka-nagara is Katwa, where Chaitanya took sannyasa (was shaven).
  14. Radha (rāṛha), the region of West Bengal west of the Ganga.
  15. Ekachakra, Nityananda's birthplace (see Chapter 5).
  16. A cloth draped around the neck is a sign of humble supplication.
  17. Ramai (Ramachandra) Pandita, Jahnava's adopted son and disciple.
  18. Jahnavi, the goddess Ganga.
  19. So in both copies; the epithets "dark, glossy" usually belong to Krishna.
  20. The second line ("sakhā tāte sarvajñātā viśvāsa vacana") is translated conjecturally.
  21. Nityananda, who also appears in the form of Ananga Manjari (cf. couplets 19 and 62).
  22. The son of Rohini is Balarama, i.e. Nityananda.
  23. The copies read "rāja-dhana māẏa/māẏaā"; read as "jāẏaā", "wife" (rhyming with "haiẏaā").
  24. The source of the quotation has not been identified. The verse turns on wordplay: "nitya" (eternal — Radha) + "ananta/ananda" (Krishna) = "Nityananda". Ananta (Shesha) is also a name of Balarama.
  25. Both copies read "dvādaśa vatsara"; the context (the stay at Mangalkot) would suggest "dvādaśa vāsara", "twelve days".
  26. A straw between the teeth is a sign of utter humility.
  27. That is, Nityananda.
  28. In couplets 88–104 "Prabhu" and "Gosani" are apparently Gopijanavallabha, carrying out Jahnava's order.
  29. The word "ākramaṇe / āntuṣane" is unclear; the general sense is given.
  30. Srimati is Jahnava.
  31. Latadhama, "abode of creepers". The name is attested in both copies (A "latādhāma.", B "latādhāma").
  32. Couplet 110 is corrupt ("se sava pāṣaṇḍīra nāma nāhi prabhu jane / karana kāraṇa dekhiveka sarvajane"); the translation is conjectural.
  33. Padmavati, Nityananda's mother.
